ov: The caterpillar of the domestic silk moth, bred in China for at least 5,000 years to make silk. It eats almost nothing but mulberry leaves, then wraps itself in a cocoon spun from a single raw-silk thread 300–900 m long. The adult moth cannot fly and depends on people to breed.

why.et: The pupae are eaten as a snack or dish in Korea (beondegi), China, Japan, Vietnam, Thailand and Assam in India.
why.dm: Fully domesticated: thousands of years of breeding have left the moth unable to fly or to breed without human help.

rg: Kept wherever silk is farmed. It was domesticated in China from the wild silk moth, which ranges from northern India to China, Korea, Japan and far-eastern Russia.
df: Almost only the leaves of white mulberry, though it will eat other mulberries and some other plants. The adult moth does not feed at all.
fx: Making one kilogram of silk takes about 4,000–7,000 cocoons.
Cocoons are boiled to unwind the silk, which kills the pupa inside; "Ahimsa silk" lets the moth emerge first.
